sources.title: Carver-Washington Half Dollar
sources.type: official coin history and legislation summary

verifiedClaims.claim: Washington was born enslaved in Virginia in 1856; Tuskegee began in 1881 with 30 students and Washington led the school.
Carver joined Tuskegee in 1896, led its agriculture department, and spent 47 years there; his work included crop rotation and teaching farming methods.
Congress authorized the Washington half dollar in 1946 and amended the program in 1951 to include Carver; the combined coin was issued from 1951 through 1954.
The coin’s reverse is an outline map of the United States; the Mint calls it the last commemorative coin before the modern program began in 1982.
